newsitem.title: USA: Merger talk again for Mobil and Amoco.
newsitem.headline: Merger talk again for Mobil and Amoco.

text.p: Merger mania again hit the U.S. refining and marketing sectors after Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette analyst John Hervey said he expected Mobil Corp and Amoco Corp to announce a fifty-fifty downstream venture.
Hervey said he was told by a senior Mobil employee that the two would announce the merger within two weeks and they believed they could save $700 million from the venture.
This pushed Mobil and Amoco shares sharply higher, while the wider market was little changed, although most major oils also saw a rise in share prices.
Mobil rose 3-9/16 to 76-7/16 and Amoco 2-1/6 to 95-13/16.
A spokesman for Mobil said his company had talked with many companies, but there was nothing new to announce.
"We are continually looking for ways to improve all our businesses around the world, including refining and marketing in the U.S.," he said.
A spokesman for Amoco said the company never commented on market rumours.
Other analysts said they had seen Hervey's comments, but until an official announcement was made, it was impossible to guess whether Mobil and Amoco were indeed close to a deal.
"This talk has been kicking around for some time," said Adam Sieminski, oil company analyst at NatWest Markets. "But as the saying goes, there is many a slip twixt cup and lip."
Talk of a downstream merger between Amoco and Mobil, the number three and number five refiners in the United States, last erupted in May.

Any joint venture would be capable of producing around two million barrels of oil per day. That is more than a joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shell Oil Co unit, Texaco Inc and Saudi Refining -- expected to be formally completed next year -- which will have capacity of 1.77 million barrels per day.
Mobil already has a refining and marketing venture with British Petroleum Co Plc in Europe, which analysts estimate generated $50 million in cost savings for Mobil in the first half of this year.
"The alliance with British Petroleum Co Plc in Europe is a case of where things were right," the Mobil spokesman said.
Analysts say there would be a good geographical fit for the two companies.

"There would be a little bit of overlap in refining for both companies, which is good, but in marketing, Mobil is a coastal company, whereas Amoco is concentrated in the central U.S.," said Sieminski.
Both companies have large refineries in the south and mid-west and Mobil has medium-sized refineries on the East and West coasts and in Louisiana.
Amoco has a small plants from Virginia to Utah, as well as its large refineries in Texas and Indiana.
"Only two people know the truth of this and they are not talking," said Sieminski of the Amoco and Mobil chief executives.
